kaps_punt: baie musiekinstrumente (stelsels) gebruik bewegings energie insette (soos blaas, klop en pluk) om hulle te laat werk; baie musiekinstrumente het dele wat kan beweeg of vibreer; musiekinstrumente produseer klank as die vernaamste uitset energie

items.bewering: 'n Musiekinstrument doen niks vanself nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Rattle (percussion instrument)' and 'Idiophone' (a player's motion drives the instrument); Science Buddies rubber-band guitar activity (sound starts only when the band is plucked). Even instruments with no player, such as wind chimes, need an input (wind), so 'niks vanself nie' holds. The next sentence correctly narrows 'iemand' to 'die meeste'.

items.bewering: By die meeste instrumente gebeur niks voordat iemand iets aan hulle doen nie.
items.bron: Same sources as above. 'Die meeste' is the right quantifier: wind-played instruments (wind chimes, aeolian harps) are the exceptions, which is why the unqualified form would be false and this one is not.

items.bewering: Jy pluk 'n snaar, of jy klop met jou hand op die drom se vel. Wat jy doen, is 'n beweging, en dit is die instrument se inset. Net soos 'n masjien het 'n instrument 'n inset nodig.
items.bron: Energy-transfer framing as in the Cognito GCSE energy-transfer notes (input energy into a device, useful and wasted outputs); Ian Perry, Cardiff University PhD thesis 2014 (orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/70916), which treats an instrument's radiated sound against its mechanical power input. Mapping checked: an instrument, like a machine, takes an energy input and gives outputs. Calling the movement itself the input is loose (strictly, energy goes in), but the next block names it bewegingsenergie, so a learner is not led astray.

items.bewering: Jy blaas oor die bokant van 'n panfluit se pype.
items.blok: Drie maniere om die beweging in te sit
items.bron: Keeping Score (San Francisco Symphony education), 'Vibrating Columns of Air with Bottle Flutes and Panpipes'; Vaia, 'pan flute': the player blows across the open top of each closed pipe.

items.bewering: Jy klop met jou hand op 'n drom se vel. Jy pluk 'n kitaar se snaar met jou vinger en laat hom los.
items.blok: Drie maniere om die beweging in te sit
items.bron: KAIST CTP431 'Fundamentals of Musical Acoustics' slides (plucking or striking excites vibration of a string or a membrane); Acoustical Society of America press-room summary on kettledrums (acoustics.org).

items.bewering: Blaas, klop en pluk is al drie dinge wat jou eie lyf doen. Jou hand of jou asem beweeg, en daardie beweging gaan by die instrument in.
items.blok: Drie maniere om die beweging in te sit
items.bron: Same sources as the items above: breath (blowing) and the hand (striking, plucking) supply the motion that sets the instrument vibrating.

items.bewering: Die energie van iets wat beweeg, noem ons bewegingsenergie.
items.blok: Drie maniere om die beweging in te sit
items.bron: Standard definition of kinetic energy as the energy of motion: Legends of Learning 'Kinetic Energy' lesson; Varsity Tutors 4th-grade energy lesson; consistent across physics references.

items.bewering: 'n Kitaar se snaar beweeg baie vinnig heen en weer net nadat jy hom gepluk het. Ons sê die snaar vibreer wanneer hy so beweeg. By 'n drom vibreer die vel waarop jy geklop het.
items.bron: KAIST CTP431 musical-acoustics slides (1D vibration of strings, 2D vibration of membranes); ASA press-room kettledrum summary (tension is the restoring force for a plucked string and a struck drumhead).

items.bewering: In albei gevalle beweeg juis die deel wat jy self aangeraak het.
items.bron: Same sources: the plucked string and the struck head are the primary vibrators. The sentence does not say ONLY that part moves (a guitar body and a drum's shell also vibrate), so it is not a false exclusivity.

items.bewering: Jy blaas oor die bokant van 'n pyp, en dan vibreer die lug binne-in daardie pyp. Die pyp self is nie die deel wat vibreer nie.
items.bron: Keeping Score panpipe lesson ('vibrating columns of air'); Neville Fletcher's wind-instrument acoustics reviews hosted by UNSW Music Acoustics (phys.unsw.edu.au/music); Kausel, Zietlow and Moore 2010 on wall vibrations: in cylindrical pipes the effect of wall vibration was not measurable, and the air column is the sound-producing vibrator. Strictly, a pipe wall can move a very little, but it is not the vibrating part that makes the sound, which is what the sentence says.

items.bewering: Die deel wat beweeg, is nie altyd die deel wat jy aanraak nie.
items.bron: Follows from the panpipe source above (you touch the pipe, the air vibrates) and the rattle sources below (you hold the shell, the seeds move). 'Nie altyd' is the correct quantifier.

items.bewering: Die kitaar: jy pluk die snaar, en die snaar beweeg heen en weer. / Die drom: jy klop op die styf gespande vel, en die vel beweeg. / Die panfluit: jy blaas oor die bokant, en die lug binne-in die pyp vibreer. / Die ratel: jy skud hom, en die saadjies binne-in klop teen die wand.
items.blok: Wat jy doen en watter deel beweeg
items.bron: Tested as a set. Guitar, drum and panpipe as above. Rattle: Wikipedia 'Rattle (percussion instrument)' and 'Idiophone', Grinnell College Musical Instruments collection and Horniman Museum object records (shaking throws the loose pellets or seeds against the shell). The contrasts the list draws hold: in two items the moving part is the part you act on, and the panpipe and rattle are both correctly shown as cases where it is not. Note for completeness: in a rattle the shell also vibrates when hit, but the list asks which part MOVES, and the seeds do.

items.bewering: Haal die deksel van 'n leë boks af. Span dan 'n rekkie oor die opening. Pluk die rekkie een keer en kyk na hom.
items.blok: Die deel moet vry wees om te beweeg
items.bron: Safety check of the hands-on step: Scouts Victoria challenge card 134 (rubber-band instrument) lists the hazards as rubber bands used as projectiles near eyes, bands looped tightly on limbs, latex allergy, and cuts from knives if a handle is cut; Pacific Science Center general guidance (adult supervision). The lesson's steps involve none of those: no cutting, no tool, an empty box, one band stretched over an opening and plucked once. The step is safe for a Grade 4 learner. A learner with a latex allergy is the only residual concern, which is a layout or teacher-note matter, not a factual fault.

items.bewering: Hy beweeg so vinnig heen en weer dat hy vaag lyk. Op dieselfde oomblik hoor jy 'n klank. Raak die rekkie nou met een vinger aan terwyl hy nog beweeg. Jy sien hoe hy ophou beweeg, en die klank hou saam met hom op.
items.blok: Die deel moet vry wees om te beweeg
items.bron: Varsity Tutors 'Explaining the vibration-sound relationship' lesson (a plucked band looks blurry and twangs; gently pressing a finger on it ends the vibration and the sound stops at the same time); Science Buddies 'Rubber Band Guitar' activity; Kennesaw State 'sound station' directions.

items.bewering: By 'n instrument werk dit net so. As die deel nie vry kan beweeg nie, kry jy byna geen klank nie.
items.blok: Die deel moet vry wees om te beweeg
items.bron: Mapping checked: the rubber band stands for a string or drumhead, and the finger for damping. Touching a vibrating object damps it and stops both motion and sound (Varsity Tutors lesson above; the guitar-string version in the same source has learners touch the string to stop it). 'Byna geen' is correctly hedged, since a damped part can still give a dull thud.

items.bewering: Jou beweging gaan by die instrument in, en 'n klank kom by hom uit. Daardie klank is die uitset waarvoor die instrument gemaak is.
items.bron: Ian Perry, Cardiff University PhD thesis 2014 (radiation efficiency as acoustic power out over mechanical power in); C.E. Gough, 'Radiation efficiencies of musical instruments', Institute of Acoustics (ioa.org.uk).

items.bewering: Nie alles wat jy insit, kom as klank by die instrument uit nie. Daarom noem ons klank die vernaamste uitset van 'n instrument en nie die enigste een nie.
items.bron: Gough, Institute of Acoustics paper on radiation efficiencies, and Perry 2014: most of an instrument's energy losses are internal damping (heat), not sound; Widener University physics lecture notes put a typical instrument's conversion to sound at about 1 per cent. So 'vernaamste' is TRUE only in the sense of 'the output it is made for', and false if read as 'the largest share of the energy'. The lesson ties it to purpose in the sentence before ('waarvoor die instrument gemaak is') and with the hair-dryer contrast after, and 'nie die enigste een nie' is correct. Bevestig as written; a reviser should not reword 'vernaamste' into anything that implies most of the energy becomes sound.

items.bewering: Dink aan 'n haardroër wat jou hare droogblaas en 'n harde geraas maak. Daardie geraas is die deel van sy uitset waarvoor hy nie gemaak is nie.
items.bron: Physics & Maths Tutor OCR GCSE flashcards 7.2 'Power and Efficiency' (hair dryer: useful = heating the air and turning the fan; wasted = sound, heating the motor, infrared); Cognito GCSE 'Energy transfer examples' (some energy carried away by sound). Mapping holds: the dryer's sound is wasted output, the instrument's sound is the intended output.

items.bewering: By die meeste masjiene is die klank nie die doel nie. By 'n instrument is die klank juis die hele doel.
items.bron: Same GCSE energy-transfer sources, which treat sound as wasted output across ordinary devices. 'Die meeste' is the correct quantifier: doorbells, alarms, sirens and loudspeakers are machines whose purpose is sound, so 'alle masjiene' would be false.

items.bewering: Die instrument se dele werk almal saam om een ding te doen. 'n Klomp dele wat so saamwerk, noem ons 'n stelsel.
items.bron: Encyclopedia.com dictionary entry 'system' ('a set of things working together as parts of a mechanism'; 'interrelated parts that function as a whole to achieve a common purpose').

items.bewering: 'n Instrument wat jy self ontwerp, het dieselfde drie dinge nodig. Jy het iets nodig om die beweging in te sit en 'n deel wat vry kan beweeg. Jy het ook 'n klank nodig wat jy kan hoor.
items.bron: Consistent with the input, vibrating part and sound output established above (Varsity Tutors and Science Buddies rubber-band activities; Keeping Score panpipe lesson).

items.bewering: 'n Radio maak ook klank, en jy druk net 'n knoppie om hom aan te sit. Binne-in die radio is daar ook 'n deel wat beweeg wanneer hy speel.
items.bron: AVIXA, 'How do speakers work'; University of Alaska Fairbanks physics web project on loudspeakers: the voice coil drives the speaker cone back and forth, pushing the air to make sound.

items.bewering: 'n Gewone radio se inset kom uit die muurprop of uit 'n battery.
items.bron: AVIXA (loudspeaker driven by an electrical signal); yours.co.uk 'best wind-up radios' and hand-crank radio guides confirm that wind-up and solar radios are the exception. 'Gewone' is the necessary qualifier and must stay, because a wind-up radio's input does come from your own movement.

items.bewering: Die verskil tussen 'n gewone radio en instrumente soos die kitaar, die drom en die panfluit lê in die inset. Hierdie instrumente se inset kom uit jou eie beweging. Daarom moet jy weer blaas, klop of pluk elke keer as jy nog 'n klank wil hê. Die radio hou aan speel solank hy sy inset kry.
items.bron: Contrast tested as a set against the lesson's own three-part frame (input, moving part, sound): both have a moving part (string, skin, air column against the speaker cone, per AVIXA) and both give sound as the intended output, so within that frame the difference is indeed the input. Naming 'instrumente soos die kitaar, die drom en die panfluit' rather than all instruments correctly avoids electric instruments. A plucked string dies away by damping (Varsity Tutors lesson above), so a new pluck is needed for a new sound; a mains or battery radio plays while powered.

items.bewering: Mense maak instrumente uit die goed wat om hulle is.
items.bron: UCT News, 'New practices reinvent traditions in bow music' (14 March 2016): musical bows 'made from grasses, sticks, and animal gut'; Wikipedia 'Uhadi musical bow' (stave from local trees such as umbangandlela, dried calabash, grass beater).

items.bewering: Die uhadi is 'n instrument van die Xhosa-mense.
items.bron: UCT News 2016 (University of Cape Town): 'the Xhosa umrhubhe mouthbow and uhadi struck bows of the Eastern Cape and Cape Town'; Wikipedia 'Uhadi musical bow', citing David Dargie, 'Xhosa Music: Its Techniques and Instruments' (1988); Wits WIReDSpace thesis 'Re-Imagining the Role of Female Players in the Making and Restoring of the UHADI Musical Bow'. The lesson does not claim the Xhosa are the only people with a gourd bow, so related bows elsewhere (such as the Zulu ugubhu) do not contradict it.

items.bewering: Dit is 'n boog met een snaar, en 'n hol kalbas is daaraan vasgemaak.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Uhadi musical bow' (large unembraced bow with one string, usinga; resonator a dried calabash, uselwa, with its seeds removed and inner walls scraped, tied to the centre of the stave), citing Dargie 1988 and T. Mandela 2005; Rhodes University Grocott's Mail 'Traditions to Treasure' (injikwe stave, usinga string, iselwa resonator).

items.bewering: Jy klop die snaar met 'n dun stingel gras of riet in jou hand. Die snaar is die deel wat beweeg wanneer jy hom klop.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Uhadi musical bow': the beater (umqungu) is made of tambookie grass (cited to T. Mandela, PhD thesis 2005), and 'the open string is either beaten or pinched ... with a scraped stick or reed' (cited to Dargie 1988). 'Gras of riet' matches both sources. UCT News 2016 confirms it is a struck bow. Only the struck string vibrates as the sound source, with the calabash as resonator.

items.bewering: Ook hierdie instrument kry sy inset uit iemand se eie beweging.
items.bron: Follows from the struck-bow sources above (UCT News 2016; Wikipedia citing Dargie 1988): the player's hand strikes the string.

items.bewering: energie: Wat nodig is om iets te laat gebeur, beweeg of werk.
items.bron: Primary-level definitions of energy as the capacity to make things move, change or do work (Legends of Learning energy lesson; headteacher.ng Primary 4 lesson note). Accurate as a Grade 4 simplification.

items.bewering: inset: Die energie wat by 'n masjien ingaan sodat hy kan werk.
items.bron: Cognito GCSE 'Energy transfer examples' (energy transferred into a device to make it work). The definition says 'masjien' while the lesson applies it to an instrument; the study text bridges this explicitly ('Net soos 'n masjien het 'n instrument 'n inset nodig'), so the entry is not false read alone.

items.bewering: uitset: Al die energie wat by 'n masjien uitkom wanneer hy werk.
items.bron: Physics & Maths Tutor OCR GCSE flashcards 7.2 and Cognito GCSE notes (outputs include both useful and wasted energy). 'Al die' is correct and is what makes 'vernaamste ... nie die enigste nie' coherent.

items.bewering: bewegingsenergie: Die energie van iets wat beweeg, soos jou hand wat klop.
items.bron: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion (Legends of Learning 'Kinetic Energy'; Varsity Tutors 4th-grade energy lesson). A knocking hand is a moving object, so the example fits.

items.bewering: vibreer: Om baie vinnig heen en weer te beweeg.
items.bron: Oxford dictionary: 'move or cause to move continuously and rapidly to and fro; oscillate'; Oxford Learner's Dictionaries: 'to move ... from side to side very quickly and with small movements'; Dictionary.com: 'to move to and fro quickly and repeatedly'.

items.bewering: stelsel: 'n Klomp dele wat saamwerk om een ding te doen.
items.bron: Encyclopedia.com dictionary entry 'system' ('a set of things working together as parts of a mechanism'; 'interrelated parts that function as a whole to achieve a common purpose').

items.bewering: uhadi: 'n Xhosa-instrument met een snaar op 'n boog en 'n hol kalbas.
items.bron: UCT News 2016 (Xhosa struck bow); Wikipedia 'Uhadi musical bow' citing Dargie 1988 (single string, bow stave, hollowed calabash resonator). True read alone.

opsomming: Elke nagaanbare bewering is bevestig (die uhadi se Xhosa-toeskrywing teen UCT en Dargie, die rekkie-proef as veilig, en die vier-item-lys as 'n stel), en die een ding wat 'n mens moet weet, is dat 'vernaamste uitset' net waar is as die uitset waarvoor die instrument gemaak is, omdat feitlik al die energie hitte word en net sowat een persent klank, wat die les korrek so stel en wat geen hersiening moet verander nie.
